course_title: Veterinary Laboratory Diagnostics for Veterinary Technologists
course_description:
This course provides theoretical and practical online training in key diagnostic skills for veterinary technicians, with a focus on diagnostic pathology and infectious diseases of small, large and exotic animals. Participants will appreciate how a diagnostic laboratory operates, understand how to prepare specimens for pathological analysis, will acquire skills for the basic interpretation of diagnostic samples, be able to describe how to effectively operate equipment and instruments commonly used in diagnostic pathology and infectious diseases, and will be able to prepare and manage cytologic, haematologic and clinical chemistry samples.

VETS3023 is designed for final year Veterinary Technology students with an interest in diagnostic laboratory work. Veterinary Technologists are vital members of veterinary diagnostic teams that work in the disciplines of anatomic pathology, clinical pathology, microbiology and parasitology. This course will provide an overview of diagnostic laboratory management aspects, including quality control and sample accession, and will also explore the various disciplines at an advanced level, building upon foundational pathobiology knowledge and skills acquired earlier in the program.

course_aims:
To introduce concepts integral to diagnostic laboratories;ﾠnamely laboratory management,ﾠsample accession and management, quality control and relevant aspects of equipment technology.

To explore advanced concepts in clinical pathology andﾠanatomic pathology at the level required of a veterinary technician aspiring entry intoﾠa career in a diagnostic services laboratory, or with an interest in laboratory diagnostics.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify blood films, and haematologic and clinical chemistry data that require referral for pathological review.
Understand the format of diagnostic submission forms and advise on appropriate collection, preservation and packaging of specimens to optimise subsequent testing and diagnosis.
Describe the generic quality control that is fundamental to diagnostic laboratories and be able to explain the relationship between quality control and the usability of clinical diagnostic data.

Identify circumstances in which sample quality may influence testing and subsequent diagnostic reliability of haematological and biochemical data and be able to formulate contingency plans to counter adverse situations.
Acknowledge and manage the risks that accompany the submittal, processing and identification of infectious agents in a diagnostic laboratory.

Deferral or extension
You may be able to defer this exam .
Students must be available for their examinations on the scheduled date, time, and campus of their course enrolment. The exam format is determined by the Course Coordinator and may include written (paper-based, online, or digital), practical, oral, or other timed assessments (such as quizzes).
If you are unable to sit for your original examination, you may be eligible for a deferred examination. To apply, you must demonstrate that unavoidable circumstances prevented you from attending your exam. If this is not possible, you can apply for a one-off discretionary deferred exam. All requests for deferred examinations MUST include supporting documentation. For more information, including acceptable evidence and application instructions, please visit my.UQ Deferring an Exam .
Please note that there are no provisions to defer an already-deferred exam. You must be available to sit your deferred examination at the allocated time.
Students who submit five or more deferral requests within a twelve-month period will be contacted with advice on the services and support available within the University.

learning_activities.topic: Revision Week Consolidation of prior knowledge in preparation for semester. Comprises pre-recorded lectures, readings and an introductory Virtual Classroom session. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Fundamentals of a Diagnostic Laboratory A pre-recorded virtual classroom session, reinforced by selected readings. Learning outcomes: L02
Laboratory Management A recorded virtual classroom session, reinforced by selected readings. Learning outcomes: L03
Haematology 1 Learn about red blood cells through virtual classes, online activities, videos, and reading materials. Learning outcomes: L01
Haematology 2 Learn about white blood cells, and platelets through virtual classes, online activities, videos, and reading materials. Learning outcomes: L01
Infectious Diseases An exploration of parasitology, microbiology and virology in a diagnostic laboratory context. Virtual classroom recording and associated readings. Learning outcomes: L02, L05
Haematology 3 Mock Haematology Exercise, discussion (recording) + answers Learning outcomes: L01
Blood Film Evaluation Exercise Week A one hour online exercise examining blood film evaluation skills, available for access during this week (week 12). Learning outcomes: L01
Urinalysis Key elements of urinalysis in a diagnostic context, including sampling and storage considerations. Learning outcomes: L02, L04
Clinical Chemistry A case study approach to clinical chemistry (readings, exercises, virtual classroom recordings, self-directed). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Histopathology Explore the role of veterinary technicians in histopathology and learn the fundamental techniques of tissue processing, staining, and slide preparation through lectures, readings, and instructional videos Learning outcomes: L02, L03
Molecular Technologies The concept of PCR and molecular-based diagnostic modalities in the laboratory. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L05
Revision Week Utilise this week to revise and prepare for the End of Semester Examination. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05
